institution: Alappuzha district AMR laboratory (District Public Health Laboratory, Alappuzha; hub General Hospital Alappuzha and 24 spoke institutions), KARS-Net district antibiogram, Department of Health Services, Kerala
citation: Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Strategic Action Plan (KARSAP), Department of Health Services, Kerala. District Antibiogram: Alappuzha, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Thrissur and Thiruvananthapuram. Chapter: Alappuzha District Antibiogram (January to December 2024), compiled by Dr Suman Susan Prakash, District Clinical Microbiologist, District Public Health Lab, Alappuzha. Thiruvananthapuram: Department of Health Services, Kerala.
reporting: Percent resistant with number tested and number resistant, by organism and specimen (pus, urine), whole district (hub and 24 spoke institutions), all locations pooled; spoke-only tables printed separately; percentages not computed when fewer than 30 isolates.
method: Conventional disc diffusion; WHONET; CLSI 2024 guidelines; one result per patient per specimen type and pathogen (1118 isolates, 946 patients).

verification.note: Tables 1, 2, 6, 8 and 10 read from the PDF text layer and compared value by value with the pages rendered at scale 2.2; every printed percentage recomputed from its printed counts (all agree). Page numbers are 1-based PDF pages of the five-district compilation.

notes: District antibiogram of secondary and primary care facilities: Alappuzha district AMR laboratory (District Public Health Laboratory) with General Hospital Alappuzha as hub and 24 spoke institutions (community and family health centres, primary health centres, taluk and district hospitals), January to December 2024; from the KARSAP compilation of five district antibiograms. All figures are percent resistant. About 87% of isolates were from outpatients, 9% inpatients and 4% ICU; tables pool all locations. Only urine and pus were processed through 2024 (blood and stool from the last quarter of 2024; no Salmonella, Shigella or Vibrio cholerae isolated). The report states 1118 isolates from 946 patients; its specimen table (Table 1) totals 1009 priority-pathogen isolates.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the 40-cell seeded sample was read blind from the page images (scale 2.5), then every one of the 59 cells, its number tested, all 7 row n values and all 12 counts (Table 1, page 17) were re-read and compared: 0 transcription errors; organism and specimen (pus, urine) correct on every row; every printed percentage agrees with its printed counts.

Cells the checks do not keep, confirmed as printed: Klebsiella ampicillin 93.2% resistant in pus (41 of 44) and 91.3% in urine (157 of 172), page 21 (intrinsic resistance flag). Also as printed and kept: P. aeruginosa pus imipenem 0.0% beside a starred tested count of 22, and percentages printed for fewer than 30 tested (E. coli pus meropenem 4, piperacillin-tazobactam 26; Klebsiella pus meropenem 6, urine meropenem 26); their numbers tested are recorded.
Table 1 gives 2 Acinetobacter urine isolates while Table 11 is headed Urine (n=0); the count of 2 is from Table 1 as printed.
